udt_struct_v0.doc:
The anchored mirror for one (asset, guest): `credited`
is the cumulative event-rebuilt total the admin has
anchored, `claimed` the cumulative paid out against it,
`last_anchor_ledger` the ledger the latest anchor read
through.
udt_struct_v0.name: Book

udt_struct_v0.doc:
The contract-side half of a shelf entry: what money and
proof need. `claim_id` / `policy_id` are the guest's
registry v2 binding (empty string = no record yet; the
guest stands on the shelf as unproven until one binds).
Resolution is a read-time act by the page against
registry v2; this contract never resolves at tip time.
udt_struct_v0.name: Guest

function_v0.doc:
The guest's keeper claims (pull, never push): pays
from the contract's balance of `asset` to the guest's
payout account, at most `credited - claimed`, under
the payout account's own authorization. The operator
cannot initiate, block selectively, or skim a claim \xe2\x80\x94
the cap is arithmetic, not permission.
function_v0.name: claim

function_v0.doc:
Leave the shelf: callable by the admin or by the
payout account itself. Closing stops new listing, not
value \xe2\x80\x94 a W address cannot be un-published, so credits
can still arrive for a closed ID; they anchor and
remain claimable on the same rule as open ones.
Nothing is seized or stranded by a close.
function_v0.name: close

function_v0.doc:
Post the anchored mirror for one (asset, guest): the
cumulative credited total rebuilt from the event
stream through `through_ledger`, with the digest of
the event batch it was rebuilt from. Monotonic: a
posting that would lower `credited`, or whose ledger
moves backwards, refuses. Re-posting the same total
is a no-op state (the anchor event still records the
check). Anchoring to an unassigned ID refuses \xe2\x80\x94 books
exist only for assigned guests (falsifier F1's
on-chain half).
function_v0.name: anchor

function_v0.doc:
Join the shelf: one posting, one ID (falsifier F2's
shape \xe2\x80\x94 a guest who needed anything deployed for them
would fail the experiment's own check). IDs are
sequential from 1; ID 0 is never assigned, so a credit
carrying ID 0 or any unassigned ID is unattributed by
definition and lands on the reconciliation's anomaly
line, never silently on a guest.
function_v0.name: assign

function_v0.doc:
Change a guest's payout account. Only the CURRENT
payout account's own authorization moves money's
destination \xe2\x80\x94 the operator cannot redirect a guest's
money, by construction.
function_v0.name: set_payout
